intro.title: Context Performance
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that demonstrates how to optimize performance when using the Context API. You'll learn to prevent unnecessary re-renders by splitting context providers and using React.memo. The core concept is understanding how context updates trigger component re-renders and applying techniques to control them. You'll work with React hooks like useContext, useState, and the React.memo higher-order component. By the end, you'll have a functional app that efficiently updates only the relevant parts of the UI when context values change.
intro.usecase: In complex React applications like e-commerce platforms or analytics dashboards, context performance optimization is crucial when multiple components depend on shared state. For example, a product filtering system where dozens of UI elements (price sliders, category checkboxes, sort dropdowns) all consume filter state from a single context. Without proper optimization, changing one filter could trigger unnecessary re-renders across the entire interface, causing laggy user interactions. Developers implement context performance patterns to ensure that only the relevant components update when context values change, maintaining smooth UX in data-heavy applications.
